overview: This Senate resolution sets up a committee of two senators to join a group from the House of Representatives in telling the President that both chambers have a quorum, meaning enough members to do business, and that Congress is ready to receive any message the President wishes to send. It is a traditional step taken at the start of every new Congress. The Senate approved it by unanimous consent on January 3, 2025.
for: Supporters say the tradition formally opens communication between the new Congress and the President.
against: Critics say the resolution is a routine formality that does not change any law or policy.
